extracted.intended_audience: readers and researchers of contemporary American short fiction; anthology readers
extracted.subtask_description: Describing editorial/selection qualities emphasized by a single-volume short-story anthology (The Best American Short Stories 2008). Captures the kinds of stories and qualities editors highlight when assembling the volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive and unforgettable stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Best American Short Stories 2008 gathers an array of inventive and unforgettable stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes stories that are inventive and memorable; this phrase is used as an overarching descriptor of the volume's contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration of contemporary topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Favorite and newcomer writers explore contemporary topics such as cloning, literary envy, cults, and teenage sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors favor work that engages with topical, contemporary issues and cultural phenomena; examples cited include cloning and teenage sex as subject matter shown in the volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of timeless subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories address timeless subjects: love, sibling rivalry, immigration, and religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alongside contemporary topics, selection values stories that handle enduring human themes, indicating balance between topicality and universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative premises and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Kevin Brockmeier's 'The Year of Silence' — an unnamed city must face the absence of all sound, followed by an excess of noise; Stephen Millhauser's 'The Wizard of West Orange' imagines Edison and his colleagues inventing machines dedicated to the sense of touch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection rewards original, high-concept premises and imaginative reworkings of historical or speculative scenarios; concrete examples on the page illustrate preference for inventive premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boldness and unsettling subject matter (including debut work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Katie Chase's bold and unsettling story, 'Man and Wife,' her first one published, brings to life an arranged marriage between a nine-year-old and a grown man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors include daring, even unsettling stories and are willing to showcase strong debut pieces; boldness of subject and provocative treatment can be a positive selection factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyrical/beautiful prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Nicole Krauss writes of an inherited desk that comes to represent the burden of memory for a poet in her beautiful story, 'From the Desk of Daniel Varsky.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic quality of writing—beauty of language and evocative prose—is noted as a reason for selection; exemplar used to signal stylistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range in narrative scale and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of these stories are immense, the so-called grand narratives of nation, race, and faith, and others are small: family stories, and stories of elective affinities...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The anthology values diversity of scale—from grand, sweeping narratives tackling large cultural questions to small, intimate domestic stories—indicating a preference for variety in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural relevance and intellectual potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The cultural relevance and intellectual potential of the short story are on display in this year's volume of the best-selling collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors stories that engage culturally and have 'intellectual potential,' i.e., material that prompts thought or has wider cultural resonance.
